title: Validate IP Address
summary: Given a string queryIP, determine if it is a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.
statement: Given a string queryIP, determine if it is a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address. Return 'IPv4' for a valid IPv4, 'IPv6' for a valid IPv6, and 'Neither' if the IP is invalid or not of either type. For IPv4, each segment must be between 0 and 255, cannot have leading zeros, and can only contain digits. For IPv6, each segment must be 1 to 4 characters long, can contain digits and letters (both uppercase and lowercase), and can have leading zeros.
constraints: Inputs contain only English letters, digits, dots, and colons; malformed lengths and empty input may occur.
IPv4 requires exactly four decimal groups in 0..255 with no leading zeros except the single digit 0.
IPv6 requires exactly eight nonempty groups of 1–4 hexadecimal characters. Leading zeros and either letter case are allowed.
For this problem, compressed :: notation and IPv4-embedded IPv6 are NOT accepted. Return IPv4, IPv6, or Neither.
hints: Validate the exact group structure before accepting individual numeric groups.
Use separate decimal and hexadecimal rules, especially for leading zeros and group counts.
IPv4: four 1–3-digit groups, no padding, value<=255. IPv6: eight 1–4-character hex groups, none empty.
Do not accept real-world IPv6 shorthand here. The exercise specifies the full eight-group notation only.
editorial: Group-count and character checks rule out empty fields, mixed notation, and invalid digits. IPv4 disallows leading zeros while IPv6 permits them. Full IPv6 notation is at most 39 characters, so longer inputs can be rejected immediately. The oracle uses two independent full-string regular expressions with explicit decimal ranges and hex grammar.

tests.explanation: Four decimal groups lie in 0..255 and have no leading zeros, so return IPv4.
Eight hexadecimal groups are present. Uppercase letters and the leading zero in 0370 are allowed for IPv6.
